problem: Existing navigation benchmarks evaluate indoor and outdoor navigation separately and mostly abstract away robot execution (discrete actions, no dynamics), so exit finding, boundary traversal, post-transition adaptation and kinodynamic/safety failures in connected indoor-to-outdoor episodes are not evaluated.
motivation: Delivery, campus security and emergency-response robots must go from buildings to streets in one continuous episode. Real robots fall, collide, and face curbs and terrain variation that sliding-agent or panorama-based benchmarks ignore. A physics-enabled benchmark with connected scenes and safety metrics is needed to expose these failures.
key_idea: Build NavVerse, an Isaac Sim benchmark of 200 indoor, outdoor and connected indoor-to-outdoor scenes with 10K verified episodes across ObjNav, VLN and the new PlaceNav task, executed by a legged robot with shared waypoint/PID/locomotion control and scored on success, efficiency and safety.
insight: Zero-shot RL, VLA and modular baselines all reach low SR (best about 11%), and the largest drop appears at the indoor-to-outdoor boundary: UniNaVid PlaceNav SR falls from 17.65 (outdoor) to 3.64 (indoor-to-outdoor). Stage-wise analysis shows 25-48% of ObjNav indoor-to-outdoor episodes never reach the outdoors, and coverage efficiency drops after exit for all methods. The feasibility study (SGImagineNav with GT goal 27.83% vs GT trajectory 100% SR) shows the execution stack is sound and that perception, goal grounding and traversability are the bottlenecks. The oracle-trajectory experiment (Spot 100% vs Turtlebot 30.75-47.5% SR) shows embodiment dynamics matter.
method: Scene construction: 100 GRScenes indoor scenes (GRUtopia), 50 Virtual Community outdoor cities (1km x 1km, Google 3D Tiles, OSM roads with 0.2m depression, terrain material classes), and 50 indoor-to-outdoor scenes made by embedding indoor layouts behind a facade opening in a building.

Outdoor enrichment: Objaverse objects (121 categories, up to 200 cars and 1000 sidewalk objects), 30 contextual object groups, and 101 Gemini-generated storefront textures extruded to 3D and placed at OSM store locations.

Episode generation: NavMesh (Recast) start/goal sampling with 5-50m paths, online verification by physics rollout of the oracle path (oracle success, duration, no fall), then VLM-refined VLN instructions (template plus keyframes) and human filtering; 10,000 episodes total (4,027 ObjNav, 2,973 PlaceNav, 3,000 VLN).
Tasks: ObjNav (136 categories), PlaceNav (17 storefront categories, e.g. restaurant, bank, no indoor-only split), and VLN with route instructions.

Executable robot interface: RGB-D 640x480 plus GT pose; waypoint, discrete or velocity actions; a shared PID waypoint follower at 50Hz feeding a learned Isaac Lab locomotion policy (flat, rough, stairs) on Spot (also Turtlebot).

Metrics: SR/SPL with 1.0+r_robot (1.6m) tolerance, Coverage Efficiency, and safety metrics Collision Rate, Average Distance to Obstacles and Navigable Surface Ratio, plus termination labels (wrong goal, fall, timeout) and stage-wise transition analysis.

setting.backbone: Baselines evaluated zero-shot: SGImagineNav (modular map-based), PoliFormer (RL transformer), UniNaVid (VLA), LongNav-R1 (VLA trained with RL on HM3D ObjNav)
setting.training_data: Benchmark paper; baselines evaluated zero-shot with no training on NavVerse (a train split of 9,100 episodes is released but not used for the reported results)
setting.observation: Forward-facing RGB-D 640x480 at 10 FPS, plus ground-truth robot base pose and camera intrinsics/transforms; no IMU
setting.action_space: Waypoint paths (x, y, yaw), discrete primitives (forward 0.25m indoor / 1.0m outdoor, rotate 30/15 degrees, converted to single-step waypoints), or body velocity commands; executed via PID plus locomotion policy
setting.privileged: none for main results (GT robot pose is provided in observation); feasibility study uses GT goal and GT trajectory for SGImagineNav only

numbers.extra: Best baseline on ObjNav; eval split has 327 ObjNav episodes (150 indoor, 82 outdoor, 95 indoor-to-outdoor); split is the NavVerse scene-disjoint Eval split

numbers_note: NavVerse is a new benchmark, so canonical names do not apply; split is the NavVerse Eval split (scene-disjoint from Train), labelled 'test'. Per-scene-type SR/SPL (indoor, outdoor, indoor-to-outdoor), difficulty, failure, and feasibility results are in the tables but only all-scene results are listed here.
results: All zero-shot baselines score low. UniNaVid (VLA) is best in task success (ObjNav SR 11.62, PlaceNav 11.38, VLN 10.67), beating SGImagineNav, PoliFormer and LongNav-R1, while SGImagineNav has the lowest collision rate. Performance collapses in indoor-to-outdoor episodes (UniNaVid PlaceNav 17.65 to 3.64 SR), with many agents failing to find the exit.
limitations: Only zero-shot evaluation of four baselines with small eval sets (900 episodes, some splits with only 55-95 episodes), so absolute numbers are noisy and no models trained on the released train split.
Single-floor scenes, limited dynamics (no pedestrians or vehicles, no interactive doors) and no outdoor-to-indoor transitions.
Provides ground-truth robot pose to the agent, and most experiments use only Spot in simulation with no real-robot evaluation.
